minutes.headline: Board heard Shady Point lake complaints, took no action, and approved a DPW union contract after executive session
minutes.summary: The meeting featured a Council on Aging annual update, a long public discussion of noise, safety and the Shady Point campground special permit, and a town manager report covering grants and bond-bill requests. The board approved a fundraiser, a police sergeant appointment, a parking rule change and, after executive session, a DPW union agreement. No decision was made on Shady Point; town counsel will be consulted.

public_comment.topic: A board member spoke on police understaffing after an accident scene with only two patrol officers.
Resident asked about the missing gilded weathervane from Town Hall and suggested an insurance claim.
Counsel for Shady Point owners, residents and neighbors spoke on noise, jet skis, safety and police details at the lake.
Resident asked for a future agenda item on special permit and entertainment license procedures, and on unused demolition capital funds for West Street buildings.

what_happened.line: The board approved a memorandum of agreement with the Laborers Local 39 DPW unit for July 1, 2018 through June 30, 2021, by roll call, all aye.
The board took no action on the Shady Point campground after long public comment; enforcement and police continue and town counsel is to be consulted.
The noise bylaw is to go to town counsel for review before coming to the board for the fall special town meeting.
The town manager reported a Green Communities grant for energy projects at town buildings and schools, and three economic development bond bill requests.
The Personnel committee recommends hiring a consultant for a compensation and classification study, which needs an appropriation at special town meeting.

why_it_matters: The DPW contract sets labor costs for three years, and the study and any new noise rules would need town meeting votes, so both can reach the town budget, mostly taxes.
Shady Point noise and safety rules remain unsettled, and police detail costs and a possible commercial kitchen's ongoing costs are open questions for the town budget.
watch_next: August 14 workshop on the earth removal permit closure process.
Town counsel's review of the noise bylaw ahead of the fall special town meeting, where a compensation study appropriation is also expected.
